record.original_question: Determine all finite universal locally toroidal polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 16 Determine all finite universal locally toroidal polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function onto {-1, 0, ..., n}, having a unique minimum element of rank -1 and a unique maximum element of rank n, such that every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 elements, P is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: for any face F of rank i-1 and any face H of rank i+1 with F < H, there are exactly two faces G of rank i with F < G < H. An abstract polytope is regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on flags. The Schläfli type {p_1, ..., p_{n-1}} of a regular polytope records the orders of the Coxeter-type relations among adjacent generators of its automorphism group; the facets of a regular polytope of type {p_1, ..., p_{n-1}} have type {p_1, ..., p_{n-2}}, and the vertex-figures have type {p_2, ..., p_{n-1}}.

A regular abstract polytope is called locally toroidal if its facets and vertex-figures are all either spherical (i.e., classical convex regular polytopes) or toroidal (i.e., regular tessellations of a torus, obtained as quotients of Euclidean regular tessellations by sublattices). Locally toroidal polytopes occur only in ranks 4, 5, and 6.

Given a Schläfli symbol of locally toroidal type together with prescribed toroidal facets and/or vertex-figures, the universal regular polytope with these data is the (unique up to isomorphism) regular polytope of that type whose automorphism group is the largest possible, i.e., for which every other regular polytope of the same type with the same facets and vertex-figures is a quotient.

Problem. Determine all finite universal locally toroidal regular abstract polytopes: for every admissible Schläfli type (in ranks 4, 5, and 6) and every admissible choice of toroidal facets and vertex-figures, decide whether the corresponding universal regular polytope is finite, and when it is finite, describe it explicitly (e.g., its automorphism group and number of flags).
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of finite universal locally toroidal regular polytopes has been the subject of extensive work by McMullen, Schulte and others, with the rank-4 and many rank-5/6 cases settled, but some cases (notably involving certain Schläfli types in ranks 5 and 6) remain unresolved. Recent works state that "much work has been done on the toroidal case and a complete classification is now within reach," indicating substantial progress but not full completion.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Locally Toroidal Regular Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey chapter on classification of locally toroidal regular polytopes; the program is incomplete in some higher-rank cases.
status_evidence.claim: The classification program for locally toroidal regular polytopes is ongoing with major progress but not fully complete.

status_evidence.title: Locally toroidal polytopes of rank 6 and sporadic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work constructing and identifying locally toroidal polytopes of rank 6 with sporadic automorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Rank 6 cases are actively being analyzed, with new finite examples discovered.
